entities.summary:
Chen Zhen (b. 170 CE, Nanyang) was a renowned explorer and navigator of the Classical era, an age of empires, philosophical inquiry, and foundational civilizations, active in Nanyang. He was a key figure associated with the Silk Road, a network of ancient trade routes that connected the East and West. Chen Zhen's expeditions played a significant role in the exchange of goods, ideas, and cultures between China and Central Asia.

Chen Zhen's contributions to the field of navigation and cartography were groundbreaking, as he developed new techniques for charting the Silk Road and mapping the regions he explored. His work on navigation and cartography helped to facilitate trade and cultural exchange between China and Central Asia, leaving a lasting legacy in the region.

Chen Zhen's significance extends beyond his own time and region, as his work on navigation and cartography contributed to the broader development of maritime trade and cultural exchange in the ancient world. His legacy can be seen in the continued importance of the Silk Road as a major trade route and cultural exchange network.

The famous quote from the Chinese historian, 'A journey of a thousand miles begins with a single step,' is attributed to Chen Zhen, emphasizing the importance of exploration and navigation in shaping the course of human history.
